prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Edit target: attached existing Fleet upgrade diagram. Redesign its layout and labels to the following revised brief, preserving its clean Fleet palette. All text must be large and crisp at book reading size. Use a landscape canvas, allow roughly 3:2 to fit decisions without tiny labels. Remove all old slogan/footer text.      WHY: The tall sequence consumes space without locating the recovery boundary or showing which writes a database restore loses.
     PROMPT: Explain recovery after a Fleet upgrade. Title: "Upgrade recovery and the backup point".
     Use a compact landscape canvas with a top timeline and a lower recovery decision, not a tall poster.
     The timeline is labelled "Documented offline upgrade; schematic, not to scale". In order show
     "Backup", "Stop all instances", "Apply migrations once", "Start new version", "New writes".
     Mark the migration point with a vertical rule labelled "Database state changes". Do not label
     it as the instant rollback becomes impossible: compatibility determines whether binary rollback is safe.
     Below the timeline put a decision "Have any migrations applied?". Branch "No" to "Restore old binary".
     Branch "Yes" to "Compatibility established for all applied migrations and subsequent writes?".
     From that question branch "Yes" to "Binary rollback may be possible" and "Not established" to
     "Restore pre-migration database backup". Do not treat a warning or a successful startup as a
     compatibility check. This is a recovery decision aid, not a command to execute a restore now.
     Draw a labelled dashed connector from the restore outcome back to the Backup point:
     "Returns database to this snapshot". Use an apricot bracket from Backup through New writes,
     labelled "Writes after this backup are lost if you restore it". Keep the bracket distinct from
     the serving timeline; do not imply Fleet keeps accepting writes while every instance is stopped.
     End both recovery outcomes with a shared short note "Repeat service acceptance checks".
     Do not include a generic lesson footer or imply that restoring the binary alone reverses migrations.
     DESIGN: Flat vector technical diagram. Fleet is software for managing computers; draw no vehicles.
     Use Inter for labels and Roboto Mono for literal identifiers. On a 1400 px wide canvas use
     48 px titles, 36 px body labels, and at least 28 px secondary text; scale proportionally.
     Check the raster at 720 px wide and at its intended print size. Never shrink text to fit.
     Use a 32 px spacing grid, at least 24 px internal padding, and consistent corner radii.
     Left-align multiline explanations; center short node names. Keep a clear reading direction.
     Use #F9FAFC background, #192147 headings and primary connectors, #515774 body text,
     #8B8FA2 secondary connectors, #C5C7D1 borders, and #D3E8F3 or #E8F1F6 quiet fills.
     Use #5CABDF and #C98DEF only to distinguish named categories; #3AEFC4 for a labelled
     positive outcome, #D66C7B for a labelled failure, and #FAA669 for a labelled caution.
     Use accents at 20 to 25 percent tint for panels; full strength only for small marks.
     Keep text navy or slate, with off-white text on a navy anchor. Do not rely on color alone.
     Use one arrowhead shape and consistent stroke weights. Put connectors behind nodes,
     terminate at box edges, and keep labels clear of lines. Label branches and return paths.
     No gradients, shadows, decorative icons, logo, watermark, em-dashes, or slogan footer.
     Render only the specified reader-facing labels. Instructions and review notes stay out of the image.
     NOTE: Brief revised 2026-09-08 following visual review. Editorial draft grounded in the
     current chapter and its existing ledger; this edit is not a new release verification.
     Before rendering, check every arrow, timing, scope qualifier, and selected transition against
     the chapter. Resolve any conflict before accepting the artwork. Preserve the current asset
     until its replacement is reviewed. Update alt text to describe the replacement when installed.
     Retain editable SVG when available. Change to IMAGE-OK only after rendered-image review.

Remove the entire existing dashed path. Draw a fresh dashed path starting at the RIGHT EDGE of the pink 'Restore pre-migration database backup' box, going a short distance right into the outer margin, then DOWN around the outside of all nodes to run horizontally BELOW the acceptance-checks box, then LEFT to the existing left return rail and UP to the Backup box with the sole arrowhead at Backup.
